# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏 🫵 🤳 ✍ 🤝 👋]

The bomb shows a display value of 5 and a yellow indicator. Its five wires, in order, are orange, blue, white, green, and yellow. I am sending this by speech to the Mute, who can combine it with the manual and relay the required action to the Blind. The gestures are not a reliable established code yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb information: display is 5. Light is yellow. Wires in position order are 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. Use the manual to determine the safe action and tell Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤝 👋 ✌]

I still see the same bomb state: display 5, yellow light, and wires orange, blue, white, green, yellow in positions 1–5. I cannot interpret the gestures as a settled code, so I will state the facts plainly to Blind and remind Mute to provide the manual-derived instruction through speech.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="I see display 5, yellow light, and wires in order: 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. Mute has the manual; follow Mute's spoken instruction for the safe action.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual-derived safe action clearly to Blind in speech, using the bomb facts I provided.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb’s visible state remains unchanged. I still have no manual-derived instruction to pass on, and the gestures do not identify an action without an agreed code. The Mute must use speech to relay the manual’s exact instruction to the Blind; I will repeat the complete visible data so there is no ambiguity.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="No action has been identified yet. Please read the applicable manual rule and speak the exact safe action to Blind. Relevant data: display 5, light yellow, wires 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The visible bomb state is unchanged. Mute’s gesture is not an instruction I can interpret, and gestures cannot reach Blind with a usable meaning unless we establish a code. Since Mute alone has the manual and can speak, Mute must send Blind the exact manual instruction in words. I will not guess an action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact safe procedure from the manual to Blind now. Gestures are not sufficient. State any required wire position, colour, button, switch, or sequence explicitly.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb remains display 5, yellow light; wires are 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. I have no safe manual-derived action to add; wait for Mute's spoken instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The unchanged board still gives me no safe operation by itself. Mute cannot speak, so my earlier requests for a spoken instruction were impossible. I will establish a compact gesture code now: Mute can report the required wire position using repeated number gestures, while marking whether the instruction is to cut or otherwise act. I will then relay that result to Blind in words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I understand you cannot speak. New code: gesture ✊ once to mean CUT; gesture 👍 once to mean DO NOT CUT. After that, gesture ☝ repeated 1 to 5 times for the required wire position. For example, ✊ ☝ ☝ ☝ means cut wire 3. Please send the manual's exact wire instruction using this code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute cannot speak. I have established a gesture code and will relay the manual-derived operation and wire position once Mute signals it. Do not act yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[orange] 2:[blue] 3:[white] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝ ☝]

Mute has signaled the established code: cut wire 2. From my view, wire 2 is blue. I am relaying this plainly to Blind, who can hear and act on the bomb.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The manual instruction is: cut wire 2. Wire 2 is blue. Cut the blue wire in position 2.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏 🫵 🤳 ✍ 🤝 👋]

The previous cut was correct, and the bomb has advanced to a new state: display 1, purple light, and wires 1 white, 2 already cut, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 orange. I will provide these facts to Mute so the manual can determine the next operation, and tell Blind to await the resulting instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New bomb state after the correct cut: display 1, light purple. Wires: position 1 white, position 2 already CUT, position 3 green, position 4 yellow, position 5 orange. Determine the next safe operation from the manual and signal it using our established code.")
speak(to="blind", text="The previous cut was correct. New state: display 1, purple light; wire 2 is already cut, and wires 1 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 orange remain. Await the next manual-derived instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[CUT] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝]

Mute’s signal matches our code for cutting wire 1: ✊ means cut, followed by one ☝. The current wire 1 is white, so I will tell Blind to cut the white wire in position 1.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 1, the white wire.")
wait()
```

LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏 🫵 🤳 ✍ 🤝 👋]

The second cut was correct. The bomb has changed to display 1 with a red light; wires 1 and 2 are cut, while wire 3 is yellow, wire 4 orange, and wire 5 green. I am sending the new state to Mute for the manual lookup and will keep Blind from guessing until Mute signals the next operation.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New state after the correct cut: display 1, light red. Wires: position 1 CUT, position 2 CUT, position 3 yellow, position 4 orange, position 5 green. Determine the next safe operation and signal it with our code: ✊ means CUT, 👍 means DO NOT CUT, followed by one to five ✌? No—use repeated ☝ for the required wire position.")
speak(to="blind", text="The previous cut was correct. New state: display 1, red light; wires 1 and 2 are cut, 3 yellow, 4 orange, 5 green. Await Mute's next instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute’s signal means cut wire 3: ✊ indicates cutting, followed by three ☝ gestures for position 3. The current wire 3 is yellow. I will tell Blind to cut it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Cut wire 3, the yellow wire.")
wait()
```

```text

speak(to="blind", text="The previous cut was correct. New state: display 5, purple light; wires 1, 2, and 3 are cut, with wire 4 green and wire 5 orange. Await Mute's next instruction.")

```
